finding: The correlation length (integral of C(lag), and the exponential decay time constant) decreases monotonically and dramatically across buffer conditions B1->B5, from ~6452 to ~196 (integral; factor ~33x), i.e. it is longest at B1 and shortest at B5. This is the correlation-length signature of a finite-size / critical slowing-down transition: the correlation length is largest at the buffer condition closest to the critical point and collapses as one moves away. The inset shows the scaling factor growing ~34x over the Bcs range 3.680->3.711, consistent with divergence near Bc.
caveats: The inset collapse uses only 5 data points; the fitted beta and Bc0 are poorly conditioned (beta~544, a overflows for the least-squares solution), so the precise collapse exponent is not reliably determined from this data. The robust, defensible statement is the monotone, multi-fold decrease of the correlation length.
The correlation curves have a finite lag window; the longest (B1) extends to lag~42181, the shortest (B5) only to ~1151, so the integral is sensitive to the lag window.
The main-figure linear fits are low-R2 because the y-values (correlation) are all clustered near 1.0; they are used only to confirm the slow monotone decay.
